titulo: Audio and captions in code: local narration, soundtrack, and karaoke
lead: The same CLI that renders also speaks and listens, all on your machine: it generates the narration with a local voice, transcribes word by word with the timing of each one, and hands that to the composition. In this lesson you build the technical side of sound: narration, a rehearsal soundtrack, and the karaoke caption that lights up each word the moment it is spoken.
objetivo: generate local narration, get the timing of each word, and render a video with audio and karaoke captions.

aprende.t: tts: text to WAV with the Kokoro voice, no cloud
transcribe: the timing of each word in a transcript.json
<audio> with id, data-start, and data-volume in the composition
Captions of up to three words that light up on the beat of the speech

hero_alt: Sound editing desk with a studio microphone on an articulated arm, closed-back headphones, and a monitor showing a waveform.

secoes.titulo: From text to video with sound
secoes.sub: Click each step. Nothing leaves your machine.

nos.detalhe: The sentence that will be spoken. The text and the choice of voice are script and sound decisions, from course 2; here it is the plumbing.

hyperframes tts uses the local Kokoro-82M model. In 0.8.176, --lang pt-br picks the pronunciation; the pf_dora voice worked on this machine (it is not in the short list from --list, which points to the 54 voices of kokoro-onnx). It downloads about 340 MB on first use.
hyperframes transcribe uses the local whisper.cpp and writes transcript.json with each word, start, and end. The small model (multilingual, ~490 MB) understands Portuguese; the .en models do not.
The kit's karaoke.py groups the words three at a time, adds the narration delay, and writes a file that the composition reads on load. Nothing is fetched from the network during the render.
<audio id> with data-start goes into the mix; data-volume lowers the soundtrack. Without an id, the audio is not mixed and the video comes out silent.

secoes.legenda: Voice, soundtrack, and mixing as a creative choice: course 2 (Production). Here, only how to put sound in the code.

secoes.titulo: Narration and the timing of each word
secoes.sub: One sentence, the local voice in Portuguese, and the transcription with timing.

blocos.conteudo:
K=~/projetos/formacao-cinema-ia-motion-v72/kit
export HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1 NO_COLOR=1
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-motion/a7; rm -rf "$E"; mkdir -p "$E"
cp -r "$K/exemplos/a7-karaoke" "$E/karaoke"; cd "$E/karaoke"
TEXTO="A voz sai do seu computador, e cada palavra sabe a hora de aparecer."
npx -y hyperframes@0.8.176 tts "$TEXTO" --voice pf_dora --lang pt-br -o narracao.wav > tts.log 2>&1; echo "tts: $?"
ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration -of csv=p=0 narracao.wav
npx -y hyperframes@0.8.176 transcribe narracao.wav -m small -l pt --json > transcricao.log 2>/dev/null; echo "transcribe: $?"
python3 -c "import json; print('palavras:', len(json.load(open('transcript.json'))))"

abas.html:
tts: 0
4.074667
transcribe: 0
palavras: 14

The second line is the narration length in seconds. The word count checks the transcript, not the text: check the words by opening transcript.json.

The default transcribe model in 0.8.176 is small.en, English only. For Portuguese, pass -m small -l pt: the multilingual small doesn't appear in the --help list (tiny.en, base.en, small.en, medium.en, large-v3), but it worked on this machine (screenshot alongside). And with --engine auto (default) the CLI uses Parakeet if it's installed and covers the language; without it, whisper.cpp.

secoes.titulo: The composition with sound and karaoke
secoes.sub: A title, the narration starting at 0.5 s, a rehearsal soundtrack at 25%, and captions generated from the transcript.

blocos.conteudo: Som no código

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""karaoke.py — turns transcript.json (word + timing) into legendas.js for the composition.

Usage:  python3 karaoke.py transcript.json --inicio 0.5 --por-linha 3 > legendas.js

--inicio     seconds at which the narration starts in the video (the <audio> data-start)
--por-linha  words per caption (default 3)
Prints to stderr: "palavras: N · legendas: M".
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys


def main():
    a = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    a.add_argument("transcript")
    a.add_argument("--inicio", type=float, default=0.0)
    a.add_argument("--por-linha", type=int, default=3)
    o = a.parse_args()
    palavras = json.load(open(o.transcript, encoding="utf-8"))
    linhas = []
    for i in range(0, len(palavras), o.por_linha):
        grupo = palavras[i:i + o.por_linha]
        linhas.append({
            "inicio": round(grupo[0]["start"] + o.inicio, 3),
            "fim": round(grupo[-1]["end"] + o.inicio, 3),
            "palavras": [{"t": p["text"], "inicio": round(p["start"] + o.inicio, 3)} for p in grupo],
        })
    # each caption leaves 0.15 s after the last word, but never after the next one enters
    for atual, prox in zip(linhas, linhas[1:] + [None]):
        atual["fim"] = round(min(atual["fim"] + 0.15, prox["inicio"]) if prox else atual["fim"] + 0.15, 3)
    print("window.LEGENDAS = " + json.dumps(linhas, ensure_ascii=False) + ";")
    print(f"palavras: {len(palavras)} · legendas: {len(linhas)}", file=sys.stderr)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

export HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1 NO_COLOR=1
cd ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-motion/a7/karaoke
# rehearsal soundtrack: a soft 8 s chord generated in ffmpeg (your real soundtrack goes in its place)

  -af "afade=t=in:d=1,afade=t=out:st=6.5:d=1.5" trilha.wav

npx -y hyperframes@0.8.176 check 2>&1 | grep -E "Check passed|✗"
npx -y hyperframes@0.8.176 render --quality draft --workers 2 --quiet --output karaoke.mp4 > render.log 2>&1

abas.rot: A bug we caught in the rehearsal
abas.html: In the first version, each caption stayed 0.15 s after the last word even when the next one had already come in: two captions overlapped in the frame. karaoke.py now closes each caption at most when the next one opens. It only showed up by looking at the frames.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after you answer.

perguntas.p: The render came out silent, but the <audio> is in the composition. What should you check first?
opcoes: Whether the audio element has an id.
Whether the soundtrack was saved as MP3 instead of WAV.
Whether the video is rendering at 30 fps.
Whether the video is longer than 5 seconds.
perguntas.explica: In HyperFrames, audio without an id does not enter the mix, and lint reports media_missing_id. It is the most common reason for a silent video.

perguntas.p: Why do the captions come from a legendas.js saved in the folder and not from a fetch at render time?
opcoes: Because the render browser cannot read JSON.
Because HyperFrames forbids .json files in the folder.
Because fetching during the render breaks repeatability.
Because the file is lighter and the render is faster.
perguntas.explica: It is the rule from lesson 1: data goes in before the render, as a file in the folder. The same legendas.js always gives the same captions.

perguntas.p: The narration starts at 0.5 s in the video. Where does that delay go?
opcoes: Only in the data-start of the audio element.
In the audio's data-start and in karaoke.py's --inicio.
In tts, with the slower --speed option.
Nowhere: the engine adjusts everything on its own.
perguntas.explica: The transcript counts time from the start of the WAV. If the audio comes in at 0.5 s, each word has to come in 0.5 s later too.

perguntas.p: Which transcribe model should you use for Portuguese narration?
opcoes: small.en, the default transcribe model in 0.8.176.
tiny.en, which is the fastest of all.
base.en, as long as you pass -l pt along with it.
perguntas.explica: The .en models only transcribe English. The multilingual small understands Portuguese; large-v3 makes fewer mistakes and takes longer.

itens.texto: tts (Kokoro) and transcribe (whisper.cpp) run on your machine, through the same CLI.
The transcript.json becomes legendas.js before the render, with the narration delay added in.
<audio> with id and data-start; data-volume for the soundtrack; the checker charges for the track.
